candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Informed Consent, printed p.22 (PDF p.25)
candidate.educational_objective: A signed form alone does not establish informed consent; unresolved client questions require clarification before the nurse verifies consent and care proceeds.

options.A: Continue because the signature confirms informed consent is complete
options.B: Pause progression, notify the appropriate provider, and ensure the client's questions are addressed before verifying consent
options.C: Explain all procedure-specific risks, benefits and alternatives independently and rely on the original signature
options.D: Ask a family member to explain the procedure so it can proceed

candidate.rationale: Informed consent is more than a signature. NCSBN 2026 expects the RN to participate in obtaining informed consent and verify that the client receives education and consents to care and procedures. The client's unresolved questions show the process is not adequately complete for the nurse to simply proceed. The nurse should pause progression, communicate the concern to the appropriate provider, and ensure questions are addressed before verifying consent rather than independently substituting for the provider responsible for procedure-specific disclosure or relying on family explanation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NCSBN explicitly includes RN participation in informed consent and verification that the client received education and consents.
candidate.source_locator: Management of Care — Informed Consent, printed p.22 (PDF p.25): identify appropriate person; describe components; participate in obtaining informed consent; verify client receives education and consents for care/procedures
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
candidate.stem: A client has signed consent for an elective procedure. During preprocedure care, the client says, ‘I signed it, but I still don't understand why I need this procedure or what the alternatives are.’ What should the nurse do?
